hook: Excerpt from the Apollo 17 Technical Crew Debriefing (January 4, 1973) in which astronauts Evans, Cernan, and Schmitt describe unusual visual phenomena observed during the mission, including a fireball with a tunnel-like afterimage and persistent light flashes that correlated with the ALFMED cosmic radiation experiment.
why_it_matters: This document establishes that all three Apollo 17 crewmembers independently observed recurring light flashes throughout the mission, with Schmitt attributing one to the lunar surface itself. The ALFMED experimental data adds a controlled dimension: flashes ceased during the blindfolded experiment interval and resumed after, suggesting the crew's perception was partially suppressible—a detail relevant to distinguishing internal (radiation-induced retinal stimulation) from external sources. Evans's description of a fireball followed by a tunnel-like visual with a receding bright spot is distinct from the flash phenomenon and documented in the same debriefing session.

key_findings.finding: Astronaut Schmitt reported nearly continuous light flashes throughout the entire Apollo 17 flight whenever the crew was dark adapted.

quotes.text: We had light flashes just about continuously during the whole flight when we were dark adapted.

key_findings.finding: Schmitt believed one of the light flashes originated on the lunar surface, distinguishing it from the others.

quotes.text: I had one which I thought was a flash on the lunar surface.

key_findings.finding: During the ALFMED experiment, when the crew wore blindfolds, the visible light flashes disappeared entirely, but resumed that same night after the blindfolds were removed—a pattern observed by all three crewmembers.

quotes.text: That one period of time when we had the blindfolds on for the ALFMED experiment there were just no visible flashes, although that evening, that night, before I went to sleep I noticed that I was seeing the light flashes again.
So, it just seemed to be that one interval either side of it where the light flash was not visible to myself or to the other two crewmen.

key_findings.finding: Astronaut Evans reported seeing a fireball whose brightness decreased, after which he observed a tunnel-like formation with a bright spot at the center and the fireball receding into the distance.

quotes.text: after the brightness of the fireball decreased, I could look back up through the rendezvous window and see what to me was kind of like a tunnel with a bright spot in the middle of the tunnel. Way down the tunnel, way back behind, I could see the fireball.

key_findings.finding: Astronaut Cernan noted that the only unusual sighting he could recall from landing or recovery was seeing an aircraft carrier superstructure, which he described as unremarkable given foggy windows.

quotes.text: The only unusual sighting I can recall during landing or recovery is when the CMP looked out the window and saw the superstructure of an aircraft carrier and said, "Oh, we've got a tin can with us."
Well, it was kind of foggy on the windows.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: Wright-Patterson AFB hosted aerospace medical and unusual phenomena research; astronaut light flash observations during spaceflight were a subject of Air Force and NASA joint scientific interest in this era.

Project Blue Book catalogued unusual aerial and luminous phenomena reported by military and government personnel; astronaut visual anomaly reports from this period were within its investigative scope, though this debriefing is a NASA document.

The ALFMED experiment directly measured cosmic radiation effects on crew vision; the Atomic Energy Commission had overlapping jurisdiction over radiation research relevant to interpreting whether the light flashes were radiation-induced retinal events.
